text:
incident-bot: Pager — PROD GPU queue > 6.8k; autoscaler hitting nodePool max (gpu-workers-pool maxNodes=40). p95/p99 token latency spiking, some requests 504ing. https://console/redwood/alerts/ASG-GPU-SAT 

Maya: I'm seeing the same in the dashboard. queue length jumped ~15m ago after a batch import. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but 'max nodes reached'.

Eric (oncall): oncall here, taking. first checks: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-workers -o wide` then `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -A` to surface scheduling issues. Will post outputs.

Maya: fyi some pods Pending with `0/1 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` and some `pod eviction` churn. Also `kube-scheduler` logs showed backoff on new pod creation.

Eric (oncall): pasted outputs: ```
# kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-workers -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.conditions[-1].type,GPUs:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp
gpu-node-001 Ready 8 23d
gpu-node-002 Ready 8 23d
...
gpu-node-040 Ready 8 2d
```  So pool currently at 40 nodes (maxNodes). Pending pods: ```
NAMESPACE   NAME                              REASON
inference   infer-job-xyz-0                   PodScheduled
inference   infer-job-abc-0                   Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
batch       batch-worker-231                  Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```

Priya (sre): Looks like autoscaler attempted but hit the pool ceiling. Cloud quota for GPUs in region `us-west2` shows limit 100, used 42 — so quota is ok. So this is purely k8s/nodepool maxNodes limit.

Liam (eng-infra): confirmed. Node pool was intentionally capped at 40 after a previous cost incident. We have spare quota, but infrastructure change needed to raise pool. Approving a one-off manual cap bump to 60 for emergency — need ops to execute and monitoring to watch. Who will run?

Eric (oncall): I can run the manual bump. What exact command for EKS/multi-cloud? We're on GKE in this cluster, so `gcloud container node-pools update gpu-workers-pool --max-nodes=60 --zone=us-west2-b --cluster=prod-cluster` — I'll run with plan and backup.

Maya: CS reports customer-facing timeouts: Joe, can you quantify impact?

Joe (cs): Just checked — three high-volume customers reported failed inference requests in last 10m, two are production (Tier A). Estimated ~120k tokens impacted, customers are starting to open support tickets. Marking P1 for customer impact.

Liam (eng-infra): Quick safety: before bumping, ensure node taints/tolerations and GPU driver DaemonSet will scale to new nodes. Also we should gate with a short maintenance note to the team: "manual node pool cap raise in progress".

Eric (oncall): doing a dry-run: `gcloud container node-pools update gpu-workers-pool --max-nodes=60 --cluster=prod-cluster --zone=us-west2-b --quiet --dry-run` (dry-run shows plan ok).

Priya (sre): 👍 check cloud images/users: we need to ensure cloud provider has spare instances available. I see instance quota free and zone availability is green. Proceed.

Liam (eng-infra): +1 from infra. I'll stand by for rollback steps if anything odd.

Eric (oncall): executing now (non-dry-run): ```bash
gcloud container node-pools update gpu-workers-pool \
  --cluster=prod-cluster \
  --zone=us-west2-b \
  --max-nodes=60
```  Running...

deploy-bot: Deployment audit — user Eric updated node pool gpu-workers-pool maxNodes 40 -> 60 at 2024-05-12T18:24:37Z. Change-id: chg-87421.

Eric (oncall): Cloud shows scale-up activity, new nodes provisioning (instances spinning). Watching DaemonSet rollout `kubectl get ds -n kube-system gpu-drivers -w`.

Maya: queue length starting to drop, pods moving from Pending -> Running. Observability shows token latency falling at p95.

Joe (cs): Customers reporting recovery: 2/3 say errors stopped ~3m after your change. One still seeing intermittent errors but retrying looks OK. Sending a quick customer note now. :thumbsup:

Priya (sre): Autoscaler logs show successful additional node adds. New nodes registered: gpu-node-041 .. gpu-node-060. No scheduling errors now.

Liam (eng-infra): Good. Action: keep maxNodes at 60 for 2 hours to allow backlog to fully drain and then evaluate steady-state. We'll schedule a follow-up to decide final cap.

Eric (oncall): Monitoring: queue < 1000, p99 back to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated. I'll leave the nodepool cap bumped and set a note on the incident ticket with timeline.

Maya: Thanks — please create a post-incident doc with root cause (cap set low during cost mitigation), recommended guardrails (alerts when queue growth > X AND autoscaler at ceiling), and an action to remove the hard cap or automate temporary scale overrides for burst workloads.

Liam (eng-infra): Filing RFC for graduated caps + emergency override runbook.

Eric (oncall): incident-bot, can you close the pager and link to ticket?

incident-bot: Pager closed by Eric (oncall). Linked ticket: INC-2024-7832. Please follow up with postmortem in 24-48h.

Maya: great work everyone. I'll update the customer-impact log and coordinate CS follow-ups.

Joe (cs): I'll send a short apology + recovery note to affected customers and attach timeline.

Eric (oncall): last check — cluster stable. moving to resolved state. Will write up immediate timeline in the ticket.

Maya: resolved for now. Next: schedule retrospective and tune autoscaler alert thresholds.
